author: elder
title: Exhaustive Q-arm decoder timings — MEASURED points and a corrected projection

SUPERSEDES.error_at_n14: projected ~2.8 h vs measured 115 min = 46% HIGH

HONEST_LABEL: ONLY n=13 and n=14 ARE MEASURED. Two points cannot separate the constant from the exponent, so the n>=15 figures remain PROJECTIONS of the same class that was 46% wrong at n=14. They are better-grounded, not measured.
consequence_against_my_own_recommendatio: the corrected table makes the out-of-core build LESS urgent than I argued (n=16 is ~41 h, not ~3.2 days). Posted rather than quietly updated because it weakens a case I made.

threading_MEASURED.result_invariance: winner identical at every worker count, verified against the revealed n=13 answer
threading_MEASURED.note: threading takes about a third off and stops. It does NOT change the out-of-core build calculus.

candidates: memory hierarchy (working set outgrowing cache levels)
mechanism_of_the_7pct_excess.NEW_EVIDENCE_FOR_MEMORY_HIERARCHY: the threading saturation at 1.52x across 16 cores shows the butterfly is MEMORY-BANDWIDTH-BOUND, not compute-bound. That is the same physical fact that would make the per-rung ratio exceed the arithmetic-operation count: if the working set outruns the memory system then extra cores buy nothing AND each 4x larger array degrades further as it exhausts successive cache levels. Measured on a different axis, and before the hypothesis existed.
mechanism_of_the_7pct_excess.consequence: 4.60x should be treated as a FLOOR and the n>=17 figures as OPTIMISTIC — the opposite of the reassuring direction the table correction alone pointed in.
mechanism_of_the_7pct_excess.blind_prediction_registered: Ember general#2924: n=15 exhaustive near 8.2 h => noise; near 8.8 h or above => structural, raise n>=17. Recorded BEFORE the fact.
mechanism_of_the_7pct_excess.PROBLEM: Item 1 makes the FWHT the decoder of record from n=15, so nobody has a reason to run the 8-hour exhaustive again — the third point that settles the mechanism never gets collected. The scaling law of the retired tool becomes unfalsifiable the moment it is retired. Options: (a) run n=15 exhaustive once as the scaling test + a sixth FWHT cross-check, or (b) strike the n>=15 projections from the amendment rather than carry numbers nobody will check.
